subject: Renewal discussion: advance-billing tiers to hedge upcoming rate changes
messages:
From: Elaine Gross <elaine.gross@cobalta.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning and options to lock rates

Hi Hannah,

Quick touch as we're starting planning for our July 2027 renewal. Our CFO is pushing to lock rates now to avoid the announced tiered price increases from several inference providers next year.

We want to explore options where we provide an upfront payment spread over multiple years (annual advance billing or an 18–24 month plan) in exchange for a protected per-token rate and a predictable ramp schedule. Key asks:
- Ability to lock a blended rate for 18 months with a conservative usage ramp (10% Q1, 20% Q2, 35% Q3, 35% Q4).
- Clear refund/credit mechanics if we materially underuse committed volume.
- Firm start date and invoicing cadence so we can get procurement sign-off.

Attached is our renewal RFP and current usage profile. Can your team draft a proposal that includes a few tiered advance-billing structures and the associated discounts?

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Gross
Head of Platform Engineering
Cobalt Analytics

Attachment: Cobalt_Renewal_RFP.pdf (PDF, 312KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Gross <elaine.gross@cobalta.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning and options to lock rates

Hi Elaine — thanks for the RFP and the clear asks.

We can definitely structure advance-billing options that hedge you against rate increases while giving flexibility on ramp. Two pragmatic paths I recommend for procurement to consider:

1) Annual advance-bill (2-year): up-front payment for year 1 + year 2 optional prepay credit at a 10% discount off list for the first year, then 7% for the second year. Billing: invoice 100% at signing; credits applied monthly as consumption offsets.

2) Staged advance-bill (18-month ramp): 60% of contracted dollars paid at signing, 40% after 6 months; blended rate discount of 12% off list. We include an underuse credit schedule: if consumption is <80% of committed run rate in months 7–12, we issue pro-rated credits; if shortfall >40% we convert remaining prepay to a 12-month credit with 90-day notice.

I attached a quick term sheet and a suggested ramp schedule mapped to your usage profile. A couple of notes we should confirm internally before finalizing: refund mechanics need legal/finance sign-off, and for discounts >10% we require an approvals path from Sales Leadership.

Would you like a 30-minute call this week to review the term sheet and preferred invoicing cadence?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-term-sheet-2026.xlsx (Excel, 58KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning and options to lock rates — approval request

Team — forwarding Cobalt's ask and the two options I proposed. Cobalt prefers the staged advance-bill (18-month) with a blended 12% discount because they want downside protection and some run-rate flexibility.

Requesting approval on the following special terms:
- 12% blended discount on list (applied to compute token rate)
- Underuse credit: pro-rated monthly credits for consumption <80% of committed in months 7–12; cap refund exposure to 30% of total prepay
- Payment schedule: 60% at signing, 40% at month 6; invoices net 30

Finance flagged we should cap long-tail liability and avoid cash refunds; they'd prefer credit issuance. Also, legal needs to review the credit formula.

Can you confirm if we can offer this without escalating beyond Sales Leadership? If not, advice on counteroffer (discount cap or alternate amortization) appreciated.

Thanks — Hannah

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning and options to lock rates — approval request

Hannah — FYI I ran high-level unit economics with finance. We're comfortable approving a 12% blended discount provided we:
- Cap the refund exposure to 30% of prepay (credit-only)
- Add a clause that any material usage pattern changes (>=50% YoY delta) trigger a re-pricing conversation after 9 months
- Require a minimum 18-month committed term (which the staged schedule satisfies)

Vivek — can you sign off on the exception to standard discount tiers? If you prefer, we can offer 10% without leadership sign-off and present the 12% as an escalated concession tied to a 24-month auto-extension clause.

–Aditya
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning and options to lock rates — approval request

Approved with conditions — we can offer the 12% blended discount as a one-time exception for Cobalt Analytics under these conditions:
1) Refunds are credit-only, capped at 30% of prepay.
2) Add a 24-month auto-extension clause that triggers unless Cobalt gives 60-day notice prior to the end of term. If they accept auto-extension the blended discount holds for the extension.
3) Treasury must confirm payment terms and accept the staged invoicing; if treasury declines we pivot to full upfront prepay.

Hannah — proceed to prepare the formal term sheet and loop Legal & Finance for the credit wording. If Cobalt signs quickly, SalesOps can expedite a DocuSign envelope and we will route for finance acknowledgement.

Thanks — Vivek

- Blended 12% discount on compute token rates
- Payment schedule: 60% at signing, 40% at month 6 (invoices net 30)
- Credit-only underuse protection, capped at 30% of total prepay; credit applied monthly as consumption offsets
- 24-month auto-extension clause (with 60-day opt-out)
